Section 579 — Cap. IX Arg.: Adam's sin remitted to all — God cannot leave anyone in that condemnation by strict right alone
Section 580 — Cap. IX Arg.: Major confirmed — Adam received; Christ obtained reconciliation for all; therefore reprobation only from final impenitence
Section 581 — Cap. IX Resp.: Major false for pagan infants — Augustine Enchiridion 99; Vasquez on infants
Section 582 — Cap. IX Resp.: as to adults — God does not damn without foresight of actual sin; reprobation as denying special grace is from liberty
Section 583 — Cap. IX Resp.: reprobation decree is secret — reprobates not left without hope of pardon merely by being reprobated
Section 584 — Cap. IX Resp. to Major's first confirmation: original sin is by contagion, not bare imputation; Adam's penitence was for himself
Section 585 — Cap. IX Resp. to Major's second confirmation: Christ obtained reconciliation for all — only individual impenitence bars participation
Section 586 — Cap. IX Resp.: no promise of faith to every adult or regenerating covenant with every infant — passing over some in original sin alone is free right; Major not confirmed
Section 587 — Cap. IX Resp. to Minor: God reprobating those in original sin alone does not deal by strict or highest right
Section 588 — Cap. IX Resp.: God confers corporal and spiritual benefits on the reprobate — therefore not strict right; false dichotomy with highest mercy
Section 589 — Cap. IX Resp.: with the non-elect God acts from philanthropy, goodness, and admirable mildness — conscience convicts innate contagion or voluntary rebellion
Section 590 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 open: God wills the saving grace of the Gospel offered promiscuously to all — Mat. 28:19; Mk 16:15; Col. 1:28
Section 591 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: Docete omnes gentes / Predicate omni creaturae — apostolic authority for the whole world; wall between Jew and Gentile down
Section 592 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: ministers must seek to bring every hearer to Christ — Augustine De correptione et gratia 15
Section 593 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: deny adversaries' corollary — reprobation of those to whom Christ ordered preaching is not only from foresight of demerits
Section 594 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: evangelizing mandate does not clash with reprobating will — passover antecedes final hardness, not from foresight of it
Section 595 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: Matt. 11:25; 13:11; Rom. 9:18 — antecedent good pleasure where the word was preached; efficacious grace prepared for some only
Section 596 — Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: physician analogy — command to preach to all does not prove God decreed to free all efficaciously
Section 597 — Cap. IX Arg. 4: God is ready to give all sufficient media to believe and convert — therefore reprobation only by consequent will after foresight of final impenitence
Section 598 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: universal sufficient grace is a slippery postulate — Vasquez grants some infants never received sufficient media of salvation
Section 599 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: infants of unbelieving idolaters — rejection without foresight of the reprobate's unbelief; Vasquez also grants some adult reprobation before foresight of sins
Section 600 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: supply of sufficient grace does not exclude antecedent reprobation — preparation of efficacious grace does, and implies election

Section 601 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: apostate angels received sufficient media yet some were elect, some reprobate — so sufficient grace to all would not prove reprobation only from foresight of final unbelief
Section 602 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol: predestination is ordination with infallible event; reprobation denies unfrustrable special operation — Bellarmine: God not bound to give sufficient grace to all
Section 603 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: Bellarmine's mediate/immediate dodge — sufficient help for an Indian or American infant in the parents cannot be explained
Section 604 — Cap. IX Arg. 4 Sol cont.: many adults lack immediate aid to believe — Bellarmine's 'posse' via creatures is a miserable defense of esse

Section 605 — Cap. IX Arg. A vocatione Evangelica: absolute antecedent election/reprobation would make indiscriminate Gospel offers a simulation — therefore reprobation only after foresight of despised grace
Section 606 — Cap. IX Sol: reprobation here means fixed decree not to give special efficacious grace — damnation from sin; denial of that grace from mere liberty of will
Section 607 — Cap. IX Sol: without simulation God can offer remission and life indiscriminately on condition of faith — reprobation decree is not 'even if Judas believes he will not be saved'
Section 608 — Cap. IX Sol: willing to save anyone if he believes is not decreeing to work faith in everyone — Remonstrants confuse the two; conditional will = faith-salvation nexus
Section 609 — Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: 'precise/absolute elect cannot be commanded to believe' misreads absolute election as cutting off means
Section 610 — Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: Peter and Paul absolutely predestined to life and to the whole series of means — will of end absolutely joined to will of means
Section 611 — Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: reprobates may be commanded to believe and offered salvation if they believe — as non-elect angels were commanded to obey
Section 612 — Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: reprobates are not required to believe a falsehood — Christ's death applies under the revealed condition of faith, not secret predestination (John 3:15–16)
Section 613 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 open: absolute reprobation not from foresight of final impenitence is said to cast perdition's cause on defect of grace — Corvinus
Section 614 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol open: reprobation does not make God or defect of grace the true cause of human perdition — the sinner with his sins is the true and sole cause
Section 615 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: equivocation on 'cause' — true/direct vs abusive/indirect; sun illuminates truly, its setting is only abusively cause of darkness
Section 616 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: special grace's gift is productive cause of salvation — its denial is not truly cause of perdition; Aristotle Metaph. 4.2

Section 617 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: 'God always ready to add further grace if well used' does not break the defense — election is absolute gift; reprobation denies efficacious grace de facto, not hypothetical gift

Section 618 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: contempt of given grace may explain withdrawal — not why special mercy that always removes contempt was never prepared; urging the non-reprobate until regeneration

Section 619 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: Corvinus's rule 'to him who does all he can by received grace, further grace is always given' does not shake absolute reprobation — no mortal ever does all he can

Section 620 — Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: Thomas — free will disordered toward evil cannot offer no impediment to grace; God sometimes converts even those who impede; the difference hangs on simple will

Section 621 — Cap. IX Arg. 7: if reprobation is antecedent and not from foresight of future impenitence, then the impenitence for which reprobates are damned flows from the reprobation decree — unjust
Section 622 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: God foresaw reprobates would be impenitent — but that foresight is not antecedent moving cause of reprobation; unbelief sprouts from the reprobate's perverse heart
Section 623 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: God elects some to be faithful and makes them so — he did not reprobate men that they might be unbelievers; Lombard Sent. 1 dist. 40–41
Section 624 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: why all reprobates become unbelieving — Augustine Ad Simpl.: nothing worse infused; only what would make better is not given; Prosper
Section 625 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: Adam's rebellion, impenitence, and unbelief are born in-house — no need to fetch such effects from divine reprobation
Section 626 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: to reprobate is to permit by denying special grace — not to pour spiritual malice; media to death are deficient evils from us, not from God
Section 627 — Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol close: theft/homicide do not precede hanging as means procured by the judge — so reprobates' sins precede damnation as presupposed matter (Cajetan)
Section 628 — Cap. IX Arg. 8: absolute reprobation not from foresight of actual sins makes God deal more rigidly with some men than with the very devils
Section 629 — Cap. IX Arg. 8: Borrius and Arminius — no one damned for original sin alone; Remonstrants at Dort: infants incapable of disobedience not punished with eternal pain
Section 630 — Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol first: from Arminian concessions — if all are made guilty of eternal death by Adam's imputed act alone, God deals more rigidly with men than with demons
Section 631 — Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol second: comparing rigor in reprobating men vs demons is inept — reprobation is denial of an undue benefit, not an act decreeing punishment
Section 632 — Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol third: foundation rotten — blessed angels elected, damned angels passed over, not from foresight of merits/rebellion but from mere liberty of will
Section 633 — Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol cont.: they wrongly slide from reprobation to damnation — two things hanging on diverse causes
Section 634 — Cap. IX Arg. 8 Sol cont.: Augustine — infants go into the mildest of all damnation, demons into the bitterest; degrees in eternal damnation unknown

Section 635 — Cap. IX Arg. 9: if creation of each is continuation of first creation, absolute reprobation not from foresight of final unbelief fights creation diametrically — creation would become a medium subordinated to damnation
Section 636 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: eternal non-election no more fights temporal creation than angelic passing-over fought angelic creation — greater difficulty with angels, seen intact
Section 637 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: Suarez and Vasquez — angels elect/non-elect with no mass of perdition; demons reprobated before any foresighted sin
Section 638 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol: creation of Judas is not a medium subordinated to his damnation — Augustine and Prosper; to create a reprobate ≠ to create that he may be damned
Section 639 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: creating Judas the reprobate is not creating him that he may be damned — as feeding a thief sentenced to die is not feeding him that he may die
Section 640 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: God creates in time those not predestined to beatitude — creation's proper end is communication of good, not damnation as intended scope
Section 641 — Cap. IX Arg. 9 Sol close: Scripture sounding as if God created some unto contumely is to be read permissively — vessels of contumely by not adding special grace
Section 642 — Cap. IX Arg. 10: if election and reprobation hang on mere liberty of will, Gospel preaching to the reprobate becomes from God's precise intention a ministry of condemnation
Section 643 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: Major's consequence invalid — not everything later done about the non-elect flows from absolute reprobation; Vasquez: some effects are of common providence
Section 644 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol: God knows Gospel benefits will harm reprobates and decreed not to add softening grace — yet preaching is not from primary intention a medium of damnation
Section 645 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: angel gifts — God foresaw abuse unto pride and rebellion, yet gifts not subordinated to ruin but to obedience and beatitude

Section 646 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: God's intention through means is judged from the nature of the means, not from the evil event he foresaw and would not hinder — same of Gospel gifts to reprobates

Section 647 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Remonstrants themselves place preaching under common providence — we grant that, adding special mercy for the elect and permission of contrary effect for the rest
Section 648 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Scripture — Gospel an odor of death from hearers' voluntary rebellion, not from God's primary intention (2 Cor. ii; Heb. ii; Acts xiii; Col. i)

Section 649 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: Gospel not administered from a precise intention of damning anyone — damnation's desert arises from neglect and contempt God foresaw and would not hinder in the reprobate

Section 650 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: two senses of 'intend' — providence disposing apt means (Adam), and predestination supplying means that secure the end (elect); Arminian third sense of intending evil by the Gospel rejected

Section 651 — Cap. IX Arg. 10 Sol cont.: means of salvation offered to reprobates are neither effects of predestination nor media of reprobation — they flow from philanthropy and more general providence; Thomas and Vasquez on the distinction
Section 652 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 (Corvinus): absolute predestination/reprobation makes baptism of many infants, by God's first intention, useless and sealing nothing — without the infants' fault
Section 653 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: absolute predestination/reprobation defined — decree to lead some by special grace to glory, deny that preparing mercy to others, and punish for final guilt of sin
Section 654 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: why baptism more useless on our view than theirs? — they also grant eternal damnation of reprobates, church-born baptism by command, and reprobation before birth
Section 655 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: remaining charge — special grace prepared for some only makes baptism useless for the rest; we deny the consequence
Section 656 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: baptism seals as Arminians allow — original-sin remission for every infant; actual-sin remission and regeneration for believers when adult
Section 657 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: Augustine, Prosper, Council of Valence on original-sin remission; baptism seals new-covenant remission of actual sins for the whole course of life (1 John i. 9)

Section 658 — Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: Augustine on sacrament preceding heart-conversion; Fulgentius — baptism suffices for infants while reason is incapable; Aquinas — Christ's passion applied by the sacrament
Section 659 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 (Corvinus): absolute reprobation blocks public prayers offered with due faith that the Word will profit all hearers
Section 660 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: right prayer for others does not require certain faith that our prayers will save them — outcomes are contingent; command to pray for all (even enemies) suffices

Section 661 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: schoolmen — four conditions for certainty of obtaining; praying for another does not always obtain; Major fails that requires certain faith prayers will profit others
Section 662 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: Minor denied — due confidence is that praying for others pleases God and we obtain as far as he sees fit; stands with our doctrine and with Arminian
Section 663 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: their conditional limitations (if they believe, if pertinacity does not hinder) we affirm too — church prayers profit all hearers under those conditions
Section 664 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: we add what they hide — God wills hearers saved if they believe, yet wills not to soften all so they believe; pray for all, treat none as reprobate
Section 665 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: who prays for one God precisely wills not to save? — secret of election/reprobation unknown; absolute reprobation is not 'damn Judas whether he believe or not'

Section 666 — Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: 'God wills all to be saved' does not overturn reprobation — election is 'I will make him saved,' not merely 'I will him to be saved'; conditional will to save stands with absolute reprobation

Section 667 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 (Corvinus): reprobation from mere liberty of will makes ministers sluggish — diligence profits only the absolutely elect; negligence harms only those absolutely to perish
Section 668 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: even if some ministers grew sluggish, the doctrine is not thereby false — abuse of Paul's teaching and of divine foresight (Augustine's monk) does not silence truth
Section 669 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: Arminius's reprobation makes ministers as sluggish — eternal foresight still fixes an immovable decree before the foundation of the world
Section 670 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: unknown elect/non-elect — Augustine: affection of charity must will all saved; rebuke all lest they perish (De corrept. et grat.)

Section 671 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: grant diligence profits only those God absolutely wills to save — still no sluggishness: honor of co-working for the elect (1 Cor. iii. 9; 2 Tim. ii. 10); woe if not preach (1 Cor. ix. 16)
Section 672 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: sloth cannot un-predestinate the elect, yet can harm them many ways — effects/benefits of predestination are to be advanced by ministers' diligence (Thomas)
Section 673 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol: 'absolutely' does not mean without means — God provides for means and end; effects arise freely and contingently (Aquinas; Paul 1 Cor. ix. 27)

Section 674 — Cap. IX Arg. 13 Sol close: negligence harms elect too; no one absolutely damned whether they repent or not; unknown whom God hardens — soft teaching (2 Tim. ii. 25); jailer analogy; absolute decrees do not cut means from end

Section 675 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): our sentence overturns religion's foundation two ways — precise election without obedience-intuit loves men more than justice and kills all religious solicitude
Section 676 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): second way — reprobation to damnation without gaze on disobedience hates the creature without justice-love and kills hope in God
Section 677 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): both inconveniences charged because we teach precise will to save before satisfaction in Christ / faith-foresight, and will to damn apart from impenitence
Section 678 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: grave charge — if our sentence uproots Christianity's foundations it must itself be uprooted; we grant their double-love foundation but deny our sentence fights it
Section 679 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: two alleged inconveniences of precise election without obedience-gaze — loves predestined more than justice; kills necessity of faith, obedience, and religious care

Section 680 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: difference from Arminius — not that elect can be saved while remaining unbelieving, but that faith/obedience is not antecedent election-motive from free will determining itself

Section 681 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: we judge faith/obedience necessary to eternal life by fixed decree — yet as special gift prepared in predestination, produced by special operation, foreseen as medium not motive

Section 682 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: first inconvenience fails — electing Peter/Paul to infallible share of Christ before foreseeing free will inclined is supreme love of justice, not loving them more than justice

Section 683 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: love of justice requires no one be loved in Christ unto actual fruitful share of salvation before persevering faith — yet may be loved unto eternal preparation of salvation before being considered as believing
Section 684 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: Arminius's further scruple — loving some unto salvation before Christ was ordained Mediator to expiate sins equals loving sinners more than justice
Section 685 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: priority of Mediator-decree vs elect-saving decree is hard speculation — execution-order is clear; eternal conception-order only God knows

Section 686 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: we confess execution-order — Christ first proposed, then apprehended by faith, then justification, sanctification, glorification; mapping a distinct decree-series in God's mind overtrusts wit

Section 687 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: first knot — Vasquez: even if Christ ordered after predestination, in execution Christ's merit causes every predestination-effect; intending a sinner's salvation with means that first satisfy justice is mercy, not loving the sinner more than justice

Section 688 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: second knot — Biel: do not posit priorities (or plural ordered acts) among these divine decrees; ranking incarnation before/after election is false speculation

Section 689 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: if we distinguish decrees by prior/posterior for weak intellect — general will to redeem via Christ (John iii. 16) and special will whereby Christ is Head of all predestined

Section 690 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: second incommodum — precise ordaining to salvation without faith/obedience-gaze does not extinguish obedience or religious care; faith required as fruit-condition, not as election-motive (Bradwardine)
Section 691 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: election decree unknown a priori — elect cannot conclude they need not obey; no election-knowledge until they feel the study of obeying God

Section 692 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: elect praxis — saints more studious of piety the more certain of election (patriarchs, Mary, apostles; 1 John iii. 3); profane presume and grow less careful, pious burn hotter

Section 693 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: reprobation half — no one appointed to damnation except from gaze on preceding sin (original, actual, or both); God hates none unto damnation without considering sin

Section 694 — Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol close: our reprobation doctrine drives no one to despair who studies to avoid sin and obey — that study is surest election-mark; those not yet feeling it must use granted means, not despair
Section 695 — Cap. X open: our sentence on reprobation is set forth and confirmed — after weighing adversaries, what our view is and on what stays it rests

Section 696 — Cap. X: to avoid calumny — our Church rejects both those who make God cause of unbelief/damnation by absolute antecedent will, and Arminian/Pelagian errors that make each man after common sufficient grace the smith of his own eternal fortune

Section 697 — Cap. X: human will leading divine will is neither worthy of God nor of Scripture — predestination is preparation of efficacious grace and glory from mere mercy, not election from foreseen faith

Section 698 — Cap. X: non-election / negative reprobation defined — not pre-damnation from foreseen final unbelief, but denial from mere will of the special mercy that softens and leads to life (Bradwardine; Rom. ix. 16, 18)

Section 699 — Cap. X: controversy-aim — show the eternal distinction of elect and non-elect in God's mind and will had no origin or motive from antecedent foresight of good acts in Peter/Paul or opposite acts in Cain/Judas

Section 700 — Cap. X controversy-sum: if in the eternal decree some were preconceived as worthier/holier and thence predestined, Arminius wins; if considered as sinners worthy of ruin and given faith by special mercy after election, we win

Section 701 — Cap. X controversy-sum continued: non-elect likewise considered sinners worthy of death, no worse in themselves, yet by freest will not dignified with the special mercy prepared for the elect — then Arminius falls, we obtain the cause
Section 702 — Cap. X: predestination already shown to depend on freest good pleasure, not antecedent human acts — remains to show the same of non-election/reprobation by gathering scattered reasons

Section 703 — Cap. X Arg. I: from adversaries' own descriptions of reprobation — absolute forescience of final impenitence/unbelief presupposes the decree to reprobate, so the decree does not flow from that foresight

Section 704 — Cap. X Arg. I: Gregory of Valencia — reprobation is the act whereby God firmly establishes to permit the reprobates' sins by not giving singular grace, exclude them from the kingdom, and punish eternally

Section 705 — Cap. X Arg. I: will to permit unbelief and deny special grace precedes absolute forescience of lasting malice — though will to punish Judas follows foresight of sin; that order is enough for our sense of reprobate

Section 706 — Cap. X Arg. I close: Augustine — God can convert any wills; he eternally established to do so in some, not in others, by mere good pleasure; Vasquez — rejection from grace has no cause in the rejected beyond first parents' sin

Section 707 — Cap. X Arg. I/II: reprobates rejected from the elect's grace not from foreseen final unbelief, but as lying in Adam's common sin — Arminius himself puts common sin before election/preterition, not final unbelief

Section 708 — Cap. X Arg. II: Arminius's Exam of Perkins — some get only sufficient grace with foresight it will be rejected; elect get efficacious grace with foresight they will believe; God decreed not to give efficacious grace to some by reprobation

Section 709 — Cap. X Arg. II close: adversaries confess an inscrutable good pleasure in preparing/not preparing efficacious grace — that pleasure precedes forescience of faith accepted or grace finally rejected; they may not affirm the reverse

Section 710 — Cap. X Arg. III: if reprobation hung on foreseen final impenitence/unbelief, no one would be reprobated except considered as dying — even as dead — because final perseverance/pertinacity is not fulfilled while we still live

Section 711 — Cap. X Arg. III: election and rejection of Jacob and Esau depicted not after life's course but before birth, when they had done neither good nor evil (Rom. ix. 11–13) — so neither elected nor rejected from Arminian foresight

Section 712 — Cap. X Arg. III: even if Rom. ix is read only of temporal honor of Jacob over Esau, by theologians' consent Paul introduced it to represent eternal predestination/reprobation — not from contrary merits of works

Section 713 — Cap. X Arg. III close: reprobation does not fall on men only after they are considered to have persevered in sins to the last breath — many consequences of reprobation reach them in this life's course

Section 714 — Cap. X Arg. III close: reprobating acts are later than final hardness yet prior to it in the order of decree — so reprobation does not follow from foreseen final unbelief but precedes that foresight (John x. 26)
Section 715 — Cap. X Arg. III close: 'not being a sheep' is antecedent to not believing — Augustine: not of my sheep because predestined to everlasting ruin, not bought for eternal life by his blood

Section 716 — Cap. X Arg. IV: if God passed over none except from foresight of sufficient grace finally despised, it would lie in each one's power to be reprobated or not — elect/reprobate difference would first arise from human wills, not diverse divine placita

Section 717 — Cap. X Arg. IV: whoever has power over the necessary antecedent has power over the consequent — if believing/not believing from free will excited by sufficient grace is the antecedent to election/reprobation, each can choose either

Section 718 — Cap. X Arg. IV: open advocates grant the consequence and find no absurdity — Lessius; but Paul refers both reprobation and election to God's antecedent will of mercy and non-mercy by good pleasure

Section 719 — Cap. X Arg. IV: Vasquez's word-refuge — reprobation-as-destination-to-punishment may be in each one's power; we mean denied preparation of sustaining/raising grace (angels and men), which Vasquez himself says is not in our power

Section 720 — Cap. X Arg. IV close: their opinion that strips God of election/reprobation liberty under pretext of foreseen faith/unbelief is not true — we say with Paul God does all by counsel of his will (Eph. i. 11)

Section 721 — Cap. X Arg. V open: to be given and not given to Christ is to be ordained or not ordained unto eternal life by predestination and preterition — and that distinction of given/not-given precedes our believing and not believing
Section 722 — Cap. X Arg. V: therefore election/predestination and preterition/reprobation do not hang on antecedent foresight of faith or unbelief — they precede such foresight
Section 723 — Cap. X Arg. V Major: John x. 28–29 — the Father gave Christ certain sheep no force can snatch; giving = electing singular persons to defend and lead infallibly to eternal life
Section 724 — Cap. X Arg. V Major: not to be given to Christ by the Father = not ordained by that gracious decree to obtain eternal life in and through Christ; John xvii. 9; Eph. i. 4–5

Section 725 — Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine — those given to Christ are ordained to eternal life, predestined and called according to purpose, none of whom perish; given = elect; not-given = reprobate/passed over

Section 726 — Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine Tract. 107/111 — world = those not in the lot of grace to be chosen out of it; those not given are those to whom Christ will not give eternal life = the passed-over alone
Section 727 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor: given/not-given distinction precedes human faith and perseverance — John vi. 37: coming to Christ depends on the Father's giving as antecedent cause

Section 728 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor: John xvii. 6, 15, 24 and Matt. xiii. 11 — order: persons given to Christ first; then Spirit opens hearts to faith; then he sustains them; God does not elect from foresight of free-will faith
Section 729 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor close: Augustine Tract. 105 — the Son is glorified so as to make the Father known to all given him; being given to Christ (that is, elected) is prior to knowing
Section 730 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor cont.: Tract. 107 — the Father’s prior giving makes them not of the world Christ does not pray for; election makes faithful, not faith elect
Section 731 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor: John x. 26 and 1 John ii. 19 — not believing / falling away is posterior to not being Christ’s sheep or of us; Arminius must say non-elect precedes unbeliever
Section 732 — Cap. X Arg. V Minor close: apostates were never given to Christ; Augustine De corr. & grat. 7 — non-perseverance follows non-election, not foresight of non-perseverance
Section 733 — Cap. X Arg. V close / Arg. VI open (Quinto): decree not to give faith is not productive cause of unbelief; Bradwardine — principate over futures and non-futures
Section 734 — Cap. X Arg. VI: principate forces the issue — non-futurity of faith in some cannot rest on bare foresight; will decrees efficacious operation or its denial
Section 735 — Cap. X Arg. VI: therefore God’s will predominates — Cain/Judas/Hymenaeus vs Peter/Paul; reprobation’s non-gift of faith precedes foreseen unbelief
Section 736 — Cap. X Arg. VI close: unbelief foreseen in negation of efficacious grace; Augustine De praedest. sanct. 6 — preparing / not preparing the will precedes foresight of faith or unbelief
Section 737 — Cap. X Arg. VII open: Arminius’s three decrees leave church-acquisition to free will; Grevinchovius and Episcopius admit redemption may apply to none / church may wholly fail
Section 738 — Cap. X Arg. VII: against Christ-death as a cast lot — Isa. liii. 10 promises Christ a church if he lays down his soul as a sacrifice
Section 739 — Cap. X Arg. VII: fulfillment of the promise not from uncertain free will but from the firmest decree and matching operation
Section 740 — Cap. X Arg. VII: Augustine De praedest. sanct. 10 — he promised from his predestination, not from our will’s power; he makes us do what he commands
Section 741 — Cap. X Arg. VII close: foresight-election leaves God’s promise, and whether Christ is Head with members, to free will — firmness is in predestination, not bare foresight
Section 742 — Cap. X Arg. VII→VIII open: if reprobation only from antecedent unbelief, all infants dying before free will—even pagans—must be elect and saved
Section 743 — Cap. X Arg. VIII: the Church never dared that — infants outside the Church born unclean and debtors of eternal death unless secret mercy intervene
Section 744 — Cap. X Arg. VIII: Augustine stops Pelagians/Semipelagians with elect/reprobate infants; De praed. sanct. 12 and De bono pers. 11 — God helps those little ones he chose before the world
Section 745 — Cap. X Arg. VIII close: Prosper — in infants neither prior merit nor future devotion is chosen; catholic sense: many die debtors of eternal death; Arminius rejected
Section 746 — Cap. X Arg. IX: from the nature of negative non-election — reprobation is denied placing of undue grace, not imposition of punishment; Rom. ix. 15
Section 747 — Cap. X Arg. IX: reprobation not a punishment — shown in reprobate angels whom Suarez, Bellarmine, Vasquez say God passed by with no merited penalty in them
Section 748 — Cap. X Arg. IX: they add God’s will as cause of angelic non-election with no cause expected from the non-elect; before any foreseen demonic sin (Suarez, Vasquez, Bellarmine)

Section 749 — Cap. X Arg. IX: objection — angelic preterition is mere denial of undue benefit, but human reprobation is true punishment from foreseen unbelief — refuted by distinguishing decrees about the fallen
Section 750 — Cap. X Arg. IX: Judas — decree to punish eternal death looks to final hardness as meritorious cause; decree not to free him by special mercy cannot look to foreseen unbelief as motive
Section 751 — Cap. X Arg. IX close: the decree to permit final hardness is reprobation itself — Rom. ix. 18; futile to refer non-preparing soft-heart grace to foreseen unbelief
Section 752 — Cap. X Arg. X open: if after sufficient grace election arose from foresight, the divide would be man’s act under indifferent grace—not a gift prepared for one and not the other
Section 753 — Cap. X Arg. X: adversaries put Peter and Judas under the same sufficient grace — free-will use separates them; that contradicts 1 Cor. iv. 7 Quis te discernit?
Section 754 — Cap. X Arg. X cont.: if 1 Cor. iv. 7 holds of gratia gratis data, much more of justifying grace and of the first grace of election to life
Section 755 — Cap. X Arg. X: Augustine De praedest. sanct. 5 — common gifts do not discern; the grace that discerns good from evil is not common; God discerns you from another
Section 756 — Cap. X Arg. X: elect/non-elect divide arises from God’s diverse decrees of preparing and giving—not from human operations about commonly offered grace; Arminius intolerable
Section 757 — Cap. X Arg. X Major/Minor: non-elect = those to whom God never destined efficacious means; many such exist; therefore many are passed by before foresight of final unbelief
Section 758 — Cap. X Arg. X Major: God knows infinite modes to turn any heart; to deny this denies omnipotence — Prov. xxi. 1; Augustine De corr. et grat. 14
Section 759 — Cap. X Arg. X: he who could bend Judas as Peter, yet destined the means to Peter not Judas, elected one and reprobated the other — Ambrose: God calls whom he deigns
Section 760 — Cap. X Arg. X: Basil and Isa. xlvi. — when God wills he saves and none resists; those not effectually called lack that unfrustrable will to convert and save
Section 761 — Cap. X Arg. X close toward Corvinus: opposite for the elect — eternal saving will proves election/preterition; foresight cannot ground either special will or its denial
Section 762 — Cap. X Arg. X / Corvinus: Contra Tilen. p.148 — not ‘God does not give, therefore he never willed to give,’ but ‘he wills gifts only to the little and obedient’
Section 763 — Cap. X Arg. X reply: question is predestinating will to do or not do — God gave Peter faith eternally willed; not giving Judas proves preterition/reprobation
Section 764 — Cap. X Arg. X: Corvinus’s ‘only to the little and obedient’ fails — same question returns; if God willed humility for Judas as for Peter, both would have it
Section 765 — Cap. X Arg. X: suspending gifts on prior littleness is Pelagian unless littleness itself is God’s special gift — Orange canon 6; preparing littleness for one is electing

Section 766 — Cap. X Arg. X close: reprobates lack saving grace because they are not what God requires — that itself proves antecedent rejection; Col. i. 12; no middle between election and reprobation

Section 767 — Cap. X Ultimum open: absolute predestination/preterition from mere divine good pleasure is not Augustine’s private opinion but received by anti-Pelagian councils — against Arminius/Corvinus

Section 768 — Cap. X Ultimum Prima: early anti-Pelagian councils did not expressly define absolute predestination — yet defined much that cannot stand if absolute gratuitous predestination is overturned; Faustus condemned

Section 769 — Cap. X Ultimum Secunda open: Orthodox predestination must be gathered from what they settled on Grace — Augustine: predestination is grace’s preparation; Vasquez: same question of grace and predestination
Section 770 — Cap. X Ultimum Secunda: true grace not according to merits cannot stand without predestination without antecedent regard to merits — Aug. De bono pers. 23
Section 771 — Cap. X Ultimum Secunda: Vasquez — Pelagians spoke the same way of predestination and of grace; God gives in time as he disposed from eternity

Section 772 — Cap. X Ultimum Secunda: who deny opposite human merits as causes why saving grace is given or withheld are held to deny that foresight difference as distinguishing conditions of election
Section 773 — Cap. X Ultimum Ultimo: Fathers before Pelagius need mild reading — election referred to foresight of merits means execution, not intention (Suarez)
Section 774 — Cap. X Ultimum: Chrysostom sometimes overstates free will, yet elsewhere grace alone; Orthodox ‘preparing for grace’ means exciting grace leads on to justification
Section 775 — Cap. X Ultimum: if Fathers teach God foresaw the faith of those destined to life, they mean merits he himself would work by predestinating grace — Aug. De praedest. sanct. 10
Section 776 — Cap. X Ultimum ratio: after these premises, Augustine’s Pauline absolute election is proved by a triple cord of three Orthodox axioms outside doubt

Section 777 — Cap. X Ultimum Major: who hold special efficacious grace prepared for some not others from mere good pleasure hold absolute election — and anti-Pelagian catholics held those three axioms with Augustine
Section 778 — Cap. X Ultimum: Major consequence — absolute predestination is mercy’s preparation of grace that leads to glory; Vossius wrongly makes efficacious grace Augustine’s peculiarity
Section 779 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1 open: Orthodox Grace of Christ is healing, regenerating, creating the good will—not merely illuminating, exciting, knocking
Section 780 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.I: Pelagius grants supernatural grace only as law and external teaching — Aug. De grat. Christi 3; Prosper De Ingratis
Section 781 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.I cont.: Pelagius then grants internal illuminating and exciting grace by persuasion — still not healing the will
Section 782 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.II: Pelagius refuses the grace that heals and turns the will by infusing faith and charity — leaves the will in indifference
Section 783 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.II: Augustine, Jerome’s Critobolus, Julian — help only to be able; Semipelagians likewise withhold the gift of willing itself
Section 784 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1: Hilary and Faustus; then Arminius/Arnoldus reject the grace that makes the good will — only sweet persuasion, event to free will
Section 785 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1 Arminius parallel: Exam. Perkins — soft persuasion not coercion; same Pelagian calumny; Corvinus leaves the will at the fork
Section 786 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1 close toward III: Hague Colloquy grants no more than Pelagius — all stall refusing the grace that by infused faith and charity makes the good will
Section 787 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: the Grace of Christ the Fathers pressed is what Pelagius and Arminius explode as free will’s coercive — Bishop of Salisbury De vera grat. Christi p.60
Section 788 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: Augustine — true grace is inspiration of love; he makes us walk and do; adjutorium whereby something is done; not only to be able but to will
Section 789 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: grace that only warns and persuades, leaving the will under free will’s dice, is law not proper grace — Aug. De grat. Christi 13–14
Section 790 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.III: not Augustine alone — Milevis can. 4, African exiles, Orange can. 4 preach creating/vivifying grace that works both to will and to do

Section 791 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1 close: illuminating/exciting grace is not the Grace of Christ Orthodoxy pressed — that grace creates the good will; received grace is not wage of a non-resisting will
Section 792 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2 open: this Grace of Christ was prepared from eternity and given in time to some, to others neither — event proves; ‘given to all but not all receive’ fails
Section 793 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: Augustine restricts vivifying grace to the predestined and purpose-called — De grat. Christi 12–13; De praedest. sanct. 9; faith a gift to some not all
Section 794 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: why not to all need not trouble the believer who holds just condemnation in Adam; Epist. 107 — Grace of God is not given to all men
Section 795 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: Epist. 107 means regenerating, sanctifying, saving grace—not Arminius’s common illuminating grace; nor ‘given because they willed’
Section 796 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2: Prosper — God foresaw whom he would give to believe; liberating grace prepared for some, not others; saving grace passes some by
Section 797 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2 close: Milevis and Orange preach justifying/converting inspiration not given promiscuously to all — Synod of African exiles in Sardinia
Section 798 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 2→3 bridge: Orthodox consent — regenerating Grace of Christ not to all but to God’s peculiar own; Propos. 3 opens on mere mercy without prior person-difference
Section 799 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: catholic doctrine — opposite always Pelagian/Semipelagian badge; they grant common offered mercy but make healing grace hang on prior merit
Section 800 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: Augustine on Pelagius — grace to the worthy; Prosper’s chronicle; Faustus — attracting mercy if given to the worthy

Section 801 — Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 3: ‘merit’ here means any prior better operation/disposition for which grace is given to one not another — then Fathers deny such prerequisite (Aug. contra 2 Epist. Pelag.)
